articles.title: Trump's China AI U-Turn After Grand Welcome To Xi Stokes Fury, Internet TORCHES 'Super Intelligence'
articles.description: US President Donald Trump’s latest comments on artificial intelligence have put his talks with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping under the spotlight. Trump said he now prefers calling artificial intelligence “superintelligence” or “SI,” arguing that the term AI makes it sound “fake.” He also claimed the United States is leading China in the technology by at least a year and said he is “not looking to open it up” because America is ahead. The remarks came after Trump and Xi discussed technology and “Super Intelligence” during their high-level talks. While Trump ruled out opening up US-China cooperation on advancing the technology, Washington and Beijing have agreed to establish channels for discussing AI-related incidents and risks, with an AI-specific dialogue planned for November.

articles.title: Hawai‘i reef sounds lured 4 to 14 times more baby fish, study finds
articles.description: In an exciting breakthrough, scientists discovered that playing sounds from thriving coral reefs significantly draws in young fish larvae. The study conducted in Kāne‘ohe Bay revealed an uptick in larval presence at sites featuring these sound recordings. However, the increased attraction was transient. This pioneering research indicates that using natural soundscapes might support reef restoration efforts, highlighting the need for further investigation into the lasting impacts on fish populations.

articles.title: Patiala University Row: Missing Girls Rumour Sparks Late-Night Protest, Police Vehicle Damaged
articles.description: A late-night protest erupted at Chitkara University in Patiala after rumours circulated on social media claiming that two female students had gone missing from the campus. Hundreds of students reportedly gathered and staged a protest, during which a police vehicle was damaged and clashes were reported between students and police personnel. Authorities reached the campus and attempted to control the situation as the protest escalated. Students also raised claims linked to an earlier alleged student suicide and circulated a video on social media that reportedly fuelled rumours about paranormal activity inside a hostel. Police officials, however, said that no confirmed information had emerged about any two missing students. DSP Sukhdev Singh said students and university representatives were questioned, but nobody could identify the names or details of the alleged missing girls. Police said the claim appeared to be circulating as a rumour and that CCTV footage would be examined to establish what actually happened on the campus. The authorities are also investigating the violence and damage reported during the protest, including the alleged assault of police personnel and damage to university infrastructure. Investigators are working to identify students who may have organised or participated in the violence. The incident has highlighted how unverified social media claims can quickly trigger panic and unrest in a university environment. Officials are expected to continue examining digital posts, CCTV footage and other available evidence to determine how the rumour originated and whether there was any factual basis behind the missing-student claim.
